newsitem.title: INDIA: India I-Sec sees 10-year government stock auction.
newsitem.headline: India I-Sec sees 10-year government stock auction.

text.p: ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said on Monday it expected the government to announce an auction of 10-year securities shortly.
In its latest debt market update, I-Sec said the first 10 364-day treasury bill auctions in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) raised over 100 billion rupees.
I-Sec is the Indian arm of investment bank J.P.Morgan.

"Assuming that the next 16 auctions raise 64 billion rupees at an average of four billion rupees per fortnight, only two more security issuances would be required to see through the balance borrowing requirement of 118.15 billion rupees, it said.
"Of these, a 10-year auction is certainly on the cards -- one would be required to set a benchmark rate before the second tranche of state development loans," the report said.
The government is also likely to issue an inflation-indexed bond, announced in the budget, in the latter half of the year after the wholesale price index adjusts for oil price increases, I-Sec said.
